answer.rationale: Primary expires in 14 days with no auto-renew while the line sits at 94% with no buffer, so a full primary switch would raise delivery risk even if memory_c2 later confirms a prior low-cost cutover was operationally clean. memory_c1 favors keeping incumbent integration; memory_c4 says market benchmarking (the low-cost quote that already meets the 18% mandate) can move the incumbent on price and terms, which is the only one-cycle move that targets TCO without a no-buffer cutover. Deferral and a second source do not secure the expiring primary. Unverified whether prior renegotiation reached an 18%-scale cut or whether that earlier onboarding would fit a 14-day, zero-buffer window.
